(a) Bands or orchestras and patron dancing shall be permitted at pouring outlets:

(b) The licensee may provide electronically amplified music or live entertainment on any patio, deck, or in any other outdoor or open air dining area immediately adjacent to the licensed premises; provided, however:
(1) Application for issuance of a temporary entertainment permit. An application for a temporary entertainment permit shall be submitted to the city clerk/treasurer with a nonrefundable payment of an administrative fee in the amount established by resolution no later than 15 days prior to the date of the event. No temporary entertainment permit shall conflict with any city sponsored special event, but may be approved upon coordination and consideration of dates, times, and schedules of activities. The following information shall be provided in the application:
a. The name, address, and telephone number of the applicant.
b. The applicant shall attach a map no smaller than 8.5 inches by 11 inches in size, clearly identifying the secured area proposed to be the location of the activity under the temporary entertainment permit. The proposed secured area shall take into account and provide for areas for public circulation around the secured area. The applicant shall describe in detail the size of the secured area proposed, and the manner and materials by which the applicant proposes to secure the area within which the activity under the temporary entertainment permit will be conducted. This description shall include the type and number of tables and seating arrangements to be located within the secured area, and describe the service area from which the provision of food and beverage services will be made.
c. The applicant shall provide such additional information as the city manager may require from time to time on application forms to be provided by the city.
(2) Administrative review and approval of a temporary entertainment permit.
a. Upon receipt of an application hereunder, the city clerk/treasurer or his designee shall note on the application the day and time of receipt.
b. The application shall be delivered to the city manager for review. In the event the city manager determines that the application is incomplete, the city manager shall return the application to the applicant, noting the nature of the deficiency. The city manager shall determine the completeness of the application within three business days of the date entered on the application by the city clerk/treasurer. In the event the applicant resubmits the application, the city clerk/treasurer or his designee shall note on the resubmitted application the day and time of receipt.
c. The city manager is authorized to approve and issue a temporary entertainment permit.
(3) Appeal of denial. Any applicant whose permit application has been denied may request a review by the city council by filing a written notice of such appeal within three business days of the notice of denial of the applicant's permit. The mayor and council shall set a hearing date within five business days of receiving such appeal request. At such a hearing, the applicant is entitled to be heard and present evidence in his behalf. The mayor and city council shall determine at the hearing whether the denial of the permit is justified. The determination by the council shall be binding upon the applicant.
(4) Time and noise limits. No licensee shall provide any electronically amplified music or live entertainment on any patio, deck, or in any other outdoor or open air dining area after 11:00 p.m., nor exceeding a volume that would be disruptive or disturbing to any neighboring residences; provided, however, that the city manager may declare that the time provided in this subsection may be extended to 1:00 a.m., of the following day on certain days, such as New Year's Eve.
(5) Compliance. Section 16-94 is complied with.
(6) Removal of tents, stages, fencing, seating, tables, and other items from secured area. The applicant shall be required to remove all tenant, stages, fencing, seating, tables, and all other items provided by or belonging to the applicant from the secured area within 24 hours of the end of the event for which the permit is issued.
(c) Failure to obtain a temporary entertainment permit or abide by the regulations for the temporary entertainment permit may result in a fine of not less than $1,000.00 per offense and possible jail time of six months. (6) All wines or malt beverages secured for event purposes must be obtained through a retail or wholesale outlet licensed in the State of Georgia.
(7) No wine or malt beverage tasting event shall last more than four hours, and no licensee may hold more than one event per week.
(8) All applicants must comply with all federal and state statutes and sections of this Code of Ordinances and other city ordinances concerning alcoholic beverages, including, but not limited to, those dealing with hours of operation, zoning, and distance requirements, excepting only the provisions of section 4-357(b).
(9) The licensee shall provide the city clerk/treasurer with written notice of the date and time of each event at least seven days prior to such event.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(H)(1); Ord. of 10-8-2013)
357:
Upon filing an application and payment of a license fee per application in the amount established by resolution, and following an investigation and criminal background check by the city manager, the city manager may issue a special event alcoholic beverage license to a qualified nonprofit civic organization. The license shall allow the applicant to serve wine and malt beverages to the public for consumption on the premises only, under the following conditions:
(1) The applicant shall be a qualified nonprofit civic organization and shall be required to submit with its application a copy of the organization's tax exempt status letter from the IRS, if applicable.
(2) The applicant shall submit with its application a statement as to the proposed location of the event, provide the name and address of the owner of the real property at which the proposed event is to occur, and shall submit the owner's written permission for the event to occur at the proposed location.
(3) The applicant must apply to the Georgia Department of Revenue for a State of Georgia One Day or Special Event Alcohol Beverage Permit, and comply with all requirements of the Georgia Department of Revenue regarding such permit.
(4) No special event may be conducted on the premises of any place of business licensed to sell distilled spirits in the unbroken container at retail.
(5) All wines or malt beverages secured for event purposes must be obtained through a retail or wholesale outlet licensed in the State of Georgia.
(6) No event shall last more than eight hours, and no licensee may hold more than two events per year.
(7) All applicants and permit holders must comply with all state statutes and sections of this Code of Ordinances and other city ordinances concerning alcoholic beverages, including, but not limited to, those dealing with hours of operation, zoning, and distance requirements, excepting only the provisions of section 4-357(b).
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(H)(2); Ord. of 10-8-2013)
358:
From time-to-time, the city council may, by resolution, allow wine and malt beverages to be brought to city sponsored events held at the Porter Memorial Gymnasium. With respect to any city-sponsored event for which such resolution is adopted, the following rules and regulations shall apply:
(1) Individuals attending the city sponsored event may bring wine and/or malt beverages to the event in the original sealed containers, to be opened only inside the Porter Memorial Gymnasium. Any individual bringing wine and/or malt beverages to the event shall transport the wine and/or malt beverage in opaque secondary containers (e.g., bags, boxes, baskets), or coolers.
(2) Individuals leaving the event may not leave the Porter Memorial Gymnasium with unsealed containers of alcohol. Bottles of wine must be securely resealed in the original container, and placed in an opaque secondary container (e.g., bags, boxes, baskets), or cooler before leaving the gymnasium. If transported in a motor vehicle, the container with the resealed bottle of wine shall be placed in a locked glove compartment, a locked trunk, or the area behind the last upright seat of a motor vehicle that is not equipped with a trunk.
(3) Individuals may not leave the Porter Memorial Gymnasium facility with an open container of malt beverage.
(4) Individuals may not carry or drink from an open container of wine and/or malt beverage while on any public street or sidewalk, or other public property, including, but not limited to, the areas surrounding the Porter Memorial Gymnasium.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(H)(4); Ord. of 10-8-2013)
361:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Authorized catered function means an event at a location not otherwise licensed for consumption of alcoholic beverages by the drink at which alcoholic beverages are furnished, for consideration, and sold, dispensed or provided free of charge to persons present at the event, by the drink, pursuant to a permit obtained under this article. The term "authorized catered function" may include a function held inside a publicly or privately owned building or structure or a function held outside such a building or structure that is located within the city limits of the City of Porterdale. An authorized catered function shall be subject to, and authorized under rules and regulations adopted by, the city.
Food caterer means any person who, for consideration, prepares food for consumption off the premises.
Licensed alcoholic beverage caterer means any person licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages by the state and who possesses a license by a local government in the state authorizing such person to sell or dispense alcoholic beverages by the drink off licensed premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(1); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
362:
An alcoholic beverage caterer license may be obtained for the purpose of selling or dispensing alcoholic beverages by the drink on premises at which authorized catered functions are to be held. Such licenses shall be annual licenses and may be obtained only by the persons, firms, or corporations already licensed by the city for the sale of alcoholic beverages at retail or by the drink. The procedures for securing such licenses and the terms thereof, including license fees, shall be as provided in this chapter. The fee for obtaining an alcoholic beverage caterer license shall be in an amount as established from time to time by resolution of the city council, provided that the total of license fees shall not exceed $5,000.0 for any one licensed location.
(1) A person or entity holding a valid license from the City of Porterdale to sell malt beverages or wine by the drink for consumption on the premises in the City of Porterdale may be issued an off-premises license which authorizes such license holder to sell malt beverages or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
(2) A person or entity holding a valid license from the city to sell malt beverages or wine by the package for consumption off the premises in the City of Porterdale may be issued an off-premises license which authorizes such license holder to sell malt beverages or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
(3) A person or entity holding a valid license from the City of Porterdale to sell distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises where sold may be issued an off-premises license which authorizes such license holder to sell distilled spirits by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(2); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
363:
Before a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer may sell or dispense alcoholic beverages at any authorized catered function, such caterer shall obtain a permit. The application for permit shall include the name of the alcoholic beverage caterer, the caterer's license number, and the date, address and time of the event. Permit applications must be filed not less than 14 days before the date of the event. No permit fee shall be charged for the alcoholic beverage caterers licensed by the city. For caterers licensed by jurisdictions other than the city, a fee of $50.00 per event shall be charged. No permit shall be issued to any person under this article who does not hold an alcoholic beverage caterer's license from a local jurisdiction in the State of Georgia. The permit shall be kept in the vehicle used to transport alcoholic beverages to the event at all times during which the permit is in effect.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(3); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
364:
(a) Caterers licensed by a jurisdiction other than the city shall maintain a record of all alcoholic beverages transported into the city for the event, and shall pay an excise tax to the city as required in this chapter. Failure to report and remit the tax within seven days of the conclusion of the event shall be grounds for denial of subsequent permits to the caterer for similar events.
(b) Caterers licensed by the city shall maintain a record of all alcoholic beverages transported for each event, by event, and shall make report and remittances of such taxes with their regular monthly reports to the city.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(4); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
365:
No alcoholic beverages shall be transported, distributed, or sold to anyone other than licensed locations in the city, except to authorized catered functions, unless otherwise authorized by this article or by Georgia State Law.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(5); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
366:
The hours and days of sale or distribution of alcoholic beverages under this article shall be the same as provided for sale by the drink under section 4-59.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(6); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
367:
No licensed alcoholic beverage caterer shall employ any person under 21 years of age to dispense, serve, sell, or handle alcoholic beverages at authorized catered functions.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(7); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
368:
All activities of alcoholic beverage caterers under this article shall be subject to and comply with the rules and regulations promulgated by the Georgia Revenue Commissioner under the authority of O.C.G.A. § 3-11-5.
(Code 2003, § 32-201(1)(I)(8); Ord. of 1-14-2014)
371:
As used in this article, the following words shall have the following meanings:
Barbering shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 43-10-1(3).
Beauty shop, beauty salon, and barber shop mean any premises where one or more individuals engage in barbering or in the occupation of a cosmetologist.
Cosmetologist shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 43-10-1(7).
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
372:
(a) A beauty shop, beauty salon, barber shop, or businesses located in and offering tours within the City of Porterdale may be issued a beer, wine and distilled spirits amenity license (hereinafter "amenity license") to serve beer, wine and/or distilled spirits as an act of hospitality and ancillary the primary business conducted. The service of an alcoholic beverage must clearly be a secondary function of the business, provided solely as an act of hospitality, and no purchase of any good or service shall be required to receive the provided beer, wine, or distilled spirits.
(b) To be eligible to apply for an amenity license, the business may not be a brewpub, hotel, lounge, private club, restaurant, special event facility or wine café, as defined in section 4-1 of the Code, respectively.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2; Ord. of 10-15-2020(1), § 1)
373:
(a) All licenses issued under this article shall constitute a mere grant or privilege to carry on or conduct the activities covered by such license and shall be subject to the terms and conditions imposed by the Charter of the City, these ordinances, the Constitution, laws and regulations of the State of Georgia, and the Constitution, laws and regulations of the United States as may be applicable thereto.
(b) All licenses issued under this article shall have printed on the face the following:
"This License is a Mere Privilege and is Subject to Being Revoked and Annulled by the Council of the City of Porterdale and is Subject to Laws, Ordinances and Regulations Hereinafter Adopted."
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
374:
(a) Application for license.
(1) Applicants for an amenity license shall execute and complete an application in such form as may be prescribed by the city clerk/treasurer from time to time containing all necessary information and representations required by this article.
(2) All applicants for licenses hereunder shall give notice of the making of an application by advertisement at least once a week for two consecutive weeks prior to the date of a public hearing on said application as provided herein in the Covington News, or other newspaper in which legal advertisements of the city are published, which notice shall contain a complete description of the location of the proposed business and shall give the name of the applicant, and, if a partnership, the names of the partners, whether limited or general, and, if a corporation, the names of the officers, and the date and time the council will hear such application. The advertisement referred to herein shall be of type not smaller than ten point capital and lower case and shall be at least a two inch by two column advertisement.
(3) Upon the filing of the application with the city clerk/treasurer, the applicant shall deposit in cash or by certified check a process fee in the amount established by resolution, which fee shall not be refundable and shall not apply against the license fee granted hereunder. This processing fee shall be in addition to the deposit of the license fee more particularly delineated in section 4-531(a).
(4) The applicant shall cause to be placed on the location of the proposed business for at least two weeks prior to the date set for a hearing on the application for a license hereunder one or more signs stating the following:
"Beer, Wine and/or Distilled Spirit Amenity License Applied For. Hearing Before the Council of the City of Porterdale, Georgia, on the ___ Day of ___, 20 ___ at ___ o'clock p.m."
The signs required by this subsection shall each not be less than 24 inches by 26 inches and shall face toward all public streets, alleys, sidewalks, or other public property adjoining the proposed location. Such signs shall be placed where they can easily be seen from all public properties adjoining the proposed location.
(5) The council shall set a date for a hearing on said application within 45 days from the date of the filing of said application.
(b) Separate application and separate license required for each location. A separate application must be made for a license and a separate license must be obtained for each location where beer, wine and/or distilled spirits may be offered as a hospitality.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
375:
(a) Occupation tax. The applicant must be a business licensed by the city, and must have paid or, if a new business, register for and pay any applicable occupation tax required under the provisions of chapter 24, article III of this Code.
(b) Age and residency requirements for licenses. No amenity license shall be issued to an applicant unless said applicant shall be:
(1) A person at least 21 years of age, who is a citizen of the United States, or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence, for a period of at least one year immediately preceding the date said license is applied for, and a resident of Butts, Henry, Jasper, Morgan, Newton, Rockdale, or Walton County;
(2) A partnership, all of whose partners are at least 21 years of age and residents of the state; or
(3) A corporation incorporated under the laws of the state or authorized by the office of the Secretary of State for the state to do business in the state. In the event an application for license is applied for by a partnership or corporation, then said applicant must name a manager, as required by section 4-26 of this Code, who shall meet the age and residency requirements of subsection (b)(1) of this section, and the requirements of section 4-26.
(c) Any licensee or person named as manager hereunder shall not have been convicted of a crime involving a violation of the ordinances of the city or any other city relating to the use, sale, taxability or possession of alcoholic beverages, or a violation of the laws of the state or of the United States pertaining to the manufacture, possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic beverages, or taxability thereof.
(d) The licensee shall be responsible for the management and operation of the business for which the license is granted.
(e) The applicant shall make a sworn statement to such applicant's qualifications in accordance with the provisions of this Code and shall place the same on file with the city clerk/treasurer for any license issued.
(f) No person shall be granted an amenity license unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the council that such person is of good moral character. The term "good moral character" means that a person has not been convicted of a felony, or any crime not a felony if it involves moral turpitude, within the past ten years. The term "conviction," as used herein, includes pleas of nolo contendere or bond forfeiture when charged with such crime.
(g) The city shall make such investigation of the qualifications of each applicant as it may deem necessary. Said investigation shall include a background check with the Georgia Crime Information Center, and submission of fingerprint identification.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
376:
All applications for licenses hereunder and consideration of the issuance of licenses shall be subject to the provisions of articles I and II of this chapter 4 of this Code, and shall be presented to the council for approval. If approved, the licenses shall be issued upon the payment of the required license fee outlined hereinafter. The failure of a licensee hereunder to comply with the laws of the State of Georgia and the rules and regulations promulgated from time to time regulating the service of alcoholic beverages on the premises by the Georgia Commissioner of Revenue, any violation of those regulations, and any violations of this Code shall subject the licensee to revocation or suspension of the license as provided for in section 4-30 of this Code.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
377:
(a) License fee.
(1) Annual license fee.
a. The annual fee for a beer, wine and/or distilled spirits amenity license shall be as established by resolution. The fee for such license shall be paid in one lump sum payment at the time of original or renewal application. In the case of a new license application, one-half of the license fee shall be paid at the time of application, and the other half shall be paid at the time of license issuance. In the case of a renewal license application, the full license fee shall be paid at the time of application.
b. No license shall be issued for less than a calendar year.
(b) Renewal application. On or before January 1 of each year, all holders of an amenity license shall make application to the council for renewal of the license, said application to be in such form and contain such information as shall from time to time be prescribed by the council and shall be accompanied by the application fee as provided herein.
(c) Issuance. If such renewal application is approved by the council, the city clerk/treasurer shall forthwith issue a license to the applicant to engage in said business for the ensuing calendar year, subject to all terms and conditions of this chapter.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
378:
When such license is suspended or revoked, as provided in this article, the holder of same shall no longer be licensed or have the right to engage in the service of alcoholic beverages until such license shall be reinstated or until such suspension expires.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)
379:
(a) Serving limitations. The licensee shall permit the service of no more than one six-ounce serving of wine, or no more than one 12-ounce serving of beer, or no more than one two-ounce serving of distilled spirits to a person within a single business day, and an individual shall not be served more than one type of alcoholic beverage.
(b) Limitation on who may serve. Service and handling of alcoholic beverages shall be made solely by the owner of the business or the manager, if any, named in the application for an amenity license. In the event a partnership or corporation holding an amenity license should change managers, said licensee immediately shall notify the city through the city clerk/treasurer or police chief of such change, and said new manager must meet all qualifications and requirements of this chapter for an individual holding an alcoholic beverage license.
(c) Availability of non-alcoholic beverages. As part of the hospitality service permitted to a licensee, the licensee shall also have available for serving and offer to serve non-alcoholic beverages.
(d) Limitation on alcoholic beverages stored on premises. A licensee shall have and store on the premises no more than three bottles of wine, one case of beer or its equivalent (i.e., 24 separate containers), or two bottles of distilled spirits at any one time.
(e) The provision of beer, wine, or distilled spirits shall be subject to the provisions of this Code and to all applicable state laws which address the use, handling and serving of alcoholic beverages, including but not limited to the limitations on the handling and serving (but not sale) of alcoholic beverages set forth in articles I and II of this chapter 4 of this Code. No one who is under 21 years of age or intoxicated may be served or consume alcoholic beverages on the premises of the licensee. It shall be the duty of the license holder or manager to enforce the limitations of this subsection (e).
(f) The licensee shall not permit the removal from the premises by a customer or guest of any opened or unopened container of alcoholic beverage.
(g) The licensee may provide the hospitality service to customers during normal business hours, and have an established closing time of no later than 10:00 p.m. The licensee shall not serve alcohol on Sundays.
(h) The licensee shall not allow any activities that would cause the business to be deemed a sexually oriented business under the provisions of article XVI of chapter 10 of this Code.
(i) Record keeping. A licensee shall maintain a record noting the date and time when any alcoholic beverage is served and type of alcoholic beverage served. The record shall be made available to the city for inspection upon request.
(Ord. of 11-05-2018(1), § 2)

383:

385:
(a) Subject to subsections (b) through (d) below, the city will not accept any applications for the retail sale of distilled spirits by the package, and no licenses for the retail sale of distilled spirits by the package shall be issued over the number of three.

In addition to the revocation of the license of any person violating the provisions of this section, that person shall be subject to punishment in the municipal court as for other violations of this Code.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
387:
(a) All holders of licenses under this article must, within nine months after the issuance of the license, open for business the establishment referred to in the license, provided, however, that for applications for a license for a premises to be constructed under the provisions of subsection 4-24(b), the nine-month period shall be extended in accordance with the provisions of subsection 119-42(b)(2)(c) governing the time period during which building permits shall remain valid or be subject to lapse. (Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
388:
(a) Liquor stores must be located at least 300 feet from churches, 600 feet from any school building, educational building, school grounds, or college campus, and 300 feet from any alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the state or any county or municipal government. The distance shall be measured by the shortest straight line possible between the nearest point on the building housing the place of business to the nearest point on the building housing such church, school building, educational building, or alcoholic treatment center, or to the nearest point on the school ground or college campus.
(b) Liquor stores must be located at least 300 feet from parks. This distance shall be measured from the front door of the liquor store to the nearest portion of the park property.
(c) Liquor stores must operate as sole tenants in a retail space of at least 4,000 square feet in size and no greater than 6,000 square feet in size. Where the space is part of a larger structure with other businesses the space for the package store shall be physically separated from the other businesses in the building by a demising wall (tenant separation wall) from floor to the underside of the roof with a minimum of a one-hour fire rating.
(d) Minimum inventory requirement upon application for license renewal.
(1) In addition to the minimum square footage requirement set forth in subsection (c) above, and as a condition to renewal of a license under this article, retail dealers for the sale of distilled spirits shall have a minimum inventory of at least $200,000.00 in distilled spirits, malt beverages or wine (where properly licensed for the sale of malt beverages and wine for consumption off premises) available for sale as of December 31 of the first year of retail operation of the licensed premises, and shall have a minimum inventory of at least $300,000.00 in distilled spirits, malt beverages or wine (where properly licensed for the sale of malt beverages and wine for consumption off premises) available for sale as of December 31 of the second year of retail operation of the licensed premises, and shall maintain at least $300,000.00 in inventory as of December 31 of each following year of retail operation of the licensed premises.

(e) Liquor stores must be located on property that is a minimum of one-half acre in size with a minimum of 250 feet of frontage on a state highway or 200 feet of frontage on a major collector street as defined in section 201 of the City of Porterdale Development Regulations.
(f) A liquor store shall not be located closer than 5,280 feet to another liquor store, regardless of jurisdiction.
(g) Liquor store buildings shall comply with overlay design regulations.
(h) Liquor store deliveries shall be made at the rear of the store building and all loading areas, dumpsters, recycling bins, and compactors shall be screened from ground view.
(i) Liquor store properties shall have no outdoor storage including the storage of shopping carts.
(j) Notwithstanding any provision of this Code to the contrary, adequate parking for a premises licensed under this article shall consist of one parking space for each 200 square feet of customer service area within the premises of applicant or license holder.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
390:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or offer for sale distilled spirits by the package within the city by means of drive-through sale. For purposes of the section, the term "drive-through sale" means the sale of distilled spirits by the package by any means that allows the customer to remain in their motor vehicles.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
391:
For licensees who wish to operate a business which conducts both the retail sale of package distilled spirits and the retail sale of package malt beverages and wine, in the case of conflict, the provisions of this article regulating the retail sale of package distilled spirits shall prevail, and compliance with those provisions, rather than the provisions applicable to the license permitting the retail sale of package malt beverages and wine, is required.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
392:
Retail package licensees shall not engage in the sale of distilled spirits except between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 11:45 p.m., Monday through Saturday, and between the hours of 12:30 p.m. and 11:30 p.m. on Sundays.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1); Ord. of 12-19-2024(2), § 3)
393:
It shall be unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage on a premises licensed for the sale of package distilled spirits. (Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
394:
(a) Every licensee shall have printed on the front of the licensed premises the name of the licensee, together with the inscription: "City of Porterdale Retail Package Sales of Distilled Spirits License No. _______" in letters not less than four inches in height.
(b) The holder of a retail distilled spirits license shall post in a conspicuous place in the licensed premises a sign printed in letters at least four inches high reading: "Sale of Alcoholic Beverages to Minors Prohibited."
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
395:
Retailers shall indicate plainly by tags or labels on the bottles or containers or on the shelf immediately below where the containers are placed the prices of all distilled spirits offered for sale.

396:
All glass surfaces forming the exterior walls of the premises shall remain unobstructed and shall provide a clear line of sight into the interior of the liquor store. No signs, window coverings, or other material shall be placed on or within ten feet of any exterior glass surfaces, except one 'open' sign of up to four square feet in area, may be placed on or near the front door. (3) Temporary signs as allowed per zoning code section 119-610.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
397:
(a) In addition to all other taxes or license fees heretofore or hereafter imposed upon retailers, dealers, or wholesalers engaged in the city and the business of selling distilled spirits, there is imposed and levied upon all here and after described retailers, dealers, or wholesalers within the city an excise tax to be computed and collected as hereinafter set forth. The taxes imposed by this section shall not be levied with respect to fortified wine as defined under O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2(9).
(b) There is levied an excise tax computed at the rate of $0.22 per liter or $0.0065 per ounce which shall be paid to the governing authority on all distilled spirits sold by wholesalers to retailers in the city. Such tax shall be paid to the city by the wholesale distributor on all distilled spirits sold to those licensed to sale package distilled spirits in the city as follows: Each wholesaler selling, shipping, or in any way delivering distilled spirits to any licensees hereunder shall collect the excise tax at the time of delivery and shall remit the same together with a summary of all deliveries to each licensee on or before the tenth day of the month following. Excise taxes received by the city after the twentieth day of the month shall be charged a ten-percent penalty. The $0.22 per liter or $0.0065 per ounce shall be prorated so that all containers of distilled spirits shall be taxed on the basis of $0.22 per liter or $0.0065 per ounce. It shall be unlawful and a violation of this section for any wholesaler to sell, ship, or deliver in any manner any distilled spirits to any retail dealer or licensee without collecting said tax. It shall be unlawful and a violation of this section for any retail dealer or licensee to possess, own, hold, store, display, or sell any distilled spirits on which such tax has not been paid. Wholesalers collecting the tax authorized herein shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and paying the amount due, if the amount is not delinquent at the time of payment. The rate of the deduction shall be at the same rate authorized for deductions from state tax under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-50, and any amendment thereto.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
398:
All sections included in article I, division 1 of article II, and article III of this chapter shall apply to the licenses and authorizations granted by this article. Any inconsistencies between the sections included in this article and article I, division 1 of article II, and article III of this chapter shall be resolved by the language of this article taking precedence over the language of articles I, division 1 of article II, and article III.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
399:
(a) With respect to this article, applications for variances from the provisions of this article and from the applicable provisions of this chapter, shall be made to, and considered by, the city council in the manner prescribed for public hearings.
(b) Appeals of city council decisions shall be made to superior court by petition for writ of certiorari in accordance with state law.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
401:
It shall be unlawful to sell, store, or offer to sell distilled spirits by the package at wholesale or retail within the city without having the appropriate license for such sale, or to carry on such activity in violation of the terms of such license or of this article.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
402:
(a) All licenses issued under this article shall constitute a mere grant or privilege to carry on or conduct the business covered by such license and shall be subject to the terms and conditions imposed by the Charter of the city, this article, and any other applicable ordinances of the city, the constitution, laws and regulations of the state, and the constitution, laws, and regulations of the United States applicable thereto.
(b) All licenses issued under this division shall have printed on the face the following:
"This License is a Mere Privilege and is Subject to Being Revoked and Annulled by the Council of the City of Porterdale and is Subject to Laws, Ordinances and Regulations Hereafter Adopted."
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
403:
(a) Generally. On or before January 1 of each year, all wholesale and retail dealers in distilled spirits sold by the package in the city shall make application to the council for a license and permit to engage in their respective businesses in the city, said application to be in such form and contain such information as shall from time to time be prescribed by the council and shall be accompanied by the application fee as provided herein.
(b) Application for retail license.
(1) Applicants for the sale of package distilled spirits licenses for sale at retail or wholesale shall execute and complete an application in such form as may be prescribed by the city clerk/treasurer from time to time containing all necessary information and representations required by this division. There shall be attached to and made a part of the application a financial statement detailing the amount of investment by the applicant, the amount and source of loans, if any, and collateral used to secure said loans, if any. This statement and the information therein shall be treated confidentially and shall be examined by the mayor and the city clerk/treasurer only.
(2) All applicants for licenses hereunder shall give notice of the making of an application by advertisement at least once a week for two consecutive weeks prior to the date of a public hearing on said application as provided herein in the Covington News, the newspaper in which legal advertisements of the city are published, which notice shall contain a complete description of the location of the proposed business and shall give the name of the applicant, and, if a partnership, the names of the partners, whether limited or general, and, if a corporation, the names of the officers, and the date and time the council will hear such application. The advertisement referred to herein shall be of type not smaller than ten point capital and lower case and shall be at least a two inch by two column advertisement.
(3) Upon the filing of the application with the city clerk/treasurer, the applicant shall deposit in cash or by certified check a process fee in the amount specified by the governing body, to cover the expense of the investigation and processing of the application, which fee shall not be refundable and shall not apply against the license fee granted hereunder.
(4) The applicant shall cause to be placed on the location of the proposed business for at least two weeks prior to the date set for a hearing on the application for retail sale of package distilled spirits license, one or more signs stating the following:
"Retail License for Sale of Distilled Spirits by the Package Applied For. Hearing Before the Council of the City of Porterdale, Georgia, on the ___ Day of _______, 20___ at _______ o'clock p.m."
The signs required by this subsection shall each not be less than 24 inches by 26 inches and shall face toward all public streets, alleys, sidewalks, or other public property adjoining the proposed location. Such signs shall be placed where they can easily be seen for all public properties adjoining the proposed location.
(5) The council shall set a date for a hearing on said application for retail sale of package distilled spirits license within 45 days from the date of the filing of said petition.
(c) Separate application and separate license required for each location. A separate application must be made for a license and a separate license to sell package distilled spirits must be obtained for each location where the same are sold.
(d) Proof of sign. Such applicant for retail sale of package distilled spirits license shall, at the public hearing on said application, submit satisfactory proof to the council that the signs required by subsection (b) of this section were properly and adequately posted and were adequate to inform the public of the pending application and the public hearing thereon.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
404:
(a) Retail licensee.
(1) Age and residency requirements for licenses. No license for the sale of package distilled spirits at retail by the package shall be issued to an applicant unless said applicant shall be:
a. A person at least 21 years of age, who is a citizen of the United States, or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence, for a period of at least one year immediately preceding the date said license is applied for, and a resident of Butts, Henry, Jasper, Morgan, Newton, Rockdale, or Walton County;
b. A partnership, all of whose partners are at least 21 years of age and residents of the state; or
c. A corporation incorporated under the laws of the state or authorized by the office of the secretary of state for the state to do business in the state.
In the event an application for license is applied for by a partnership or corporation, then said applicant must name a manager, as required by section 4-26, who shall meet the age and residency requirements of subsection (a)(1)a. of this section, and the requirements of section 4-26.
(2) Any licensee or person named as manager hereunder shall not have been convicted of a crime involving a violation of the ordinances of the city or any other city relating to the use, sale, taxability or possession of alcoholic beverages, or a violation of the laws of the state of the United States pertaining to the manufacture, possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic beverages, or taxability thereof;
(3) The licensee shall be responsible for the management and operation of the business for which the license is granted.
(4) The applicant shall make a sworn statement to such applicant's qualifications in accordance with the provisions of this division and shall place the same on file with the city clerk/treasurer for any licenses issued.
(5) No person shall be granted a license to engage in the sale of package distilled spirits at retail unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the council that such person is of good and moral character. The term "good moral character" means that a person has not been convicted of a felony, or any crime not a felony if it involves moral turpitude, within the past ten years. The term "conviction," as used herein, includes pleas of nolo contendere or bond forfeiture when charged with such crime.
(6) The city shall make such investigation of the qualifications of each applicant as it may deem necessary.
(b) Wholesale licenses. Licenses to sell package distilled spirits at wholesale shall be issued only to those parties who are licensed by the state to sell and distribute package distilled spirits at wholesale. Application for such license shall be made with the city clerk/treasurer.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
405:
(a) Authority to issue licenses. All applications for licenses hereunder shall be presented to the council for approval, and, if approved, the licenses shall be issued upon the payment of the required license fee and bond outlined herein. The failure of a licensee to comply with the laws of the state and the rules and regulations promulgated from time to time regulating the sale of package distilled spirits by the commissioner of revenue of the state and any violation of these regulations shall subject the licensee to revocation of the license.
(b) Issuance. If such application is approved by the mayor and city council, the city clerk/treasurer shall forthwith issue a license and permit to the applicant to engage in said business for the ensuing calendar year, or remaining portion thereof, subject to all terms and conditions of this division.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
406:
(a) The annual business license fee for retail sale of package distilled spirits dealers, whose place of business is located within the city, shall be as prescribed by the governing body.
(b) The annual business license fee for package distilled spirits wholesaler dealers doing business within the city shall be as prescribed by the governing body.
(c) Said license fees shall be paid annually in advance.
(d) No license shall be issued for less than a calendar year, or the remainder thereof; provided, however, that if an application is made for a license after June 30 in any calendar year, the license fee shall be 50 percent of the annual license fee for the remainder of the calendar year. If a license is revoked or surrendered before the expiration of a calendar year, the holder thereof shall not be entitled to receive any refund of the license fee paid.
(e) The license fee schedule is on file in the office of the city clerk/treasurer.
(f) License fee. The applicant for a wholesale sale of package distilled license shall pay the city clerk/treasurer at the time of such license being issued the sum specified by the governing authority.
(g) Annual renewal. All licensees hereunder shall be required to renew their license annually with the city clerk/treasurer, on the forms provided by the city.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))
407:
When such license and permit is suspended or revoked, as provided in this chapter, the holder of same shall no longer be licensed or have the right to engage in the business of selling package distilled spirits either at wholesale or at retail until such license shall be reinstated or until such suspension expires.
(Ord. of 7-21-2022(1))

411:
This chapter may be cited as the "City of Porterdale Animal Control Regulations."
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
412:
It is the purpose of this chapter to minimize health hazards of animals, and to provide a healthier atmosphere in which the citizens may enjoy their pursuits and rights in their individual properties.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
413:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned animal means any domestic animal or livestock unattended or not cared for in excess of 36 hours.
Adequate food means sufficient quantity of non-contaminated and nutritionally healthy sustenance, appropriate to the animal, or at the direction of a licensed veterinarian, sufficient to prevent starvation, malnutrition, or risk to the animal's health. Garbage, spoiled, rancid or contaminated food is not adequate food.
Adequate shelter means protective cover appropriate for the species and adequate space to maintain the animal in good health and prevent pain, suffering or a significant risk to the animal's health. Adequate shelter shall consist of a completely enclosed structure with three to four sides with a door opening, a constructed floor, and a roof. Adequate shelter shall be clean, dry and compatible with current weather and age, size, species and condition of the animal. The structure shall be of sufficient size to allow the animal to stand, turn around, lie down and go in and out of the structure comfortably. Adequate shelter must be compatible with the number of animals on the property.
(1) "Adequate shelter" includes, but is not limited to:
a. Sufficient coverage and insulation to protect from extreme hot and cold temperatures;
b. Sufficient protection from the elements to keep the animal dry;
c. Sufficient shade and ventilation to prevent overheating and/or dehydrating; and
d. Adequate bedding or resting area suitable for the animal.
(2) Materials not suitable for shelters include, but are not limited to:
a. Inadequately insulated containers;
b. Plastic kennels or airline-type animal shipping crates;
c. Metal drums;
d. Abandoned or parked vehicles;
e. Uncovered porches or decks;
f. Lean-tos;
g. Any other structure that fails to provide sufficient protection from the elements.
Adequate veterinary care means care from or under the direction of a veterinarian and necessary to maintain health, or to prevent suffering from:
(1) Infections;
(2) Parasites;
(3) Disease; or
(4) Any other condition/injury where withholding or neglecting to provide such care would:
a. Endanger the health or welfare of the animal; or
b. Promote the spread of diseases.
Adequate water means potable water in adequate supply.
Adult means a person at least 18 years of age.
Animal means any vertebrate, domestic and wild, male and female, singular or plural.
Animal control means the county animal control department, a department of the county government.
Animal control board means a board consisting of six members who are residents of the county, are duly appointed by the county board of commissioners, who carry out the duties and responsibilities of an animal control board as described in O.C.G.A. § 4-8-20, et seq., and who serve in such capacity at the pleasure of the county board of commissioners.
Animal control officer means an individual authorized by animal control to aid in the administration and enforcement of this chapter. Each such individual shall be deemed a dog control officer pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 4-8-22.
Animal establishment means an animal facility and services location, including, but not limited to, pet dealer, kennel, grooming shop, auction, or performing animal exhibition; any facility operated, owned or maintained by a humane society, animal welfare society or other nonprofit for the welfare, protection and humane treatment of animals; or other facility engaged in handling animals, excluding licensed vets and veterinary clinics and hospitals.
Animal shelter means a facility operated by a government for impounding or caring for animals.
Animal under restraint means:
(1) Any animal controlled within the property of its owner;
(2) Any animal secured by a leash with a collar, or enclosed by way of a fence or other enclosure;
(3) Any animal at heel or beside a competent person and obedient to the person's commands; or
(4) Any animal inside a vehicle driven or parked on the streets.
At-large means any animal not under control as provided in this chapter.
Auction means any place where animals are regularly bought, sold or traded, except for facilities otherwise defined in this chapter. Individual sales of animals by owners are not auctions.
Classified dog means a dog classified as a dangerous or vicious dog per this chapter.
Certificate means a certificate issued at time of vaccination, by a licensed veterinarian, with the license number, name and address of the dog or cat's owner and date of vaccination.
Cruelty means act, omission or neglect whereby pain, suffering, maiming or death may be caused or permitted.
Dangerous dog means any dog that:
(1) Causes a substantial puncture of a person's skin by teeth without causing serious injury; a nip, scratch, or abrasion shall not be sufficient to classify as dangerous under this subsection;
(2) Aggressively attacks in a manner that causes a person to reasonably believe the dog posed an imminent threat of serious injury to such person or another person although no injury occurs; barking, growling, or showing of teeth shall not be sufficient to classify a dog dangerous; or
(3) While off the owner's property, kills a pet; provided, however, this shall not apply where death is caused by a dog working or training as a hunting, herding, or predator control dog.
Dangerous Dog Control Law means O.C.G.A. § 4-8-20 et seq., incorporated herein and made a part by reference.
Dog means any domesticated species of the canine genus.
Domestic animals mean:
(1) Cats and dogs;
(2) Domesticated species of fowl and livestock; and
(3) Ferrets, rabbits, guinea pigs, or other animals commonly kept as pets and not classified by the state of Georgia as a wild or exotic animal.
EAID means an electronic animal identification device: microchip or similar device.
Feral means wild or untamed state due to birth or reversion to wild state from domestication.
Fowl means any warm-blooded, feathered, flying or non-flying animal.
Humane manner means care of an animal to include, but not be limited to, adequate heat, ventilation, sanitary shelter, wholesome fresh food, and access to potable water at all times, consistent with normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, species and breed.
Impoundment means taking physical control of an animal by animal control officers or others empowered to act by law or ordinance and subsequent transportation of such animal to the animal control facility.
Kennel means any establishment, other than an animal shelter, where dogs or cats are maintained for boarding, holding, training, or similar purposes for a fee or compensation.
Livestock means hooved animals such as bovines, swine, equines, sheep, goats, mules, other grazing animals, ratites, and non-traditional livestock not limited to, farmed deer.
Neutered means rendered permanently incapable of sexual reproduction, sterilized.
Nuisance means animal which:
(1) Damages property other than the property of the owner;
(2) Soils, defiles or defecates on property other than the owner of the animal; however, if the owner immediately removes any feces, the animal shall not constitute a nuisance;
(3) Disturbs trash or other refuse, causes unsanitary, dangerous or offensive conditions;
(4) Causes a disturbance by excessive barking or other noise making, habitually or continually yowling, crying or screaming or as further described hereinafter;
(5) Molests, attacks or interferes with persons on public or private property; or
(6) Chases vehicles or attacks other animals.
Obstruction of officer means obstruction, interference, or hindrance of an animal control officer or law enforcement officer in the discharge of official duties.
Owner means any person who owns, harbors, keeps and maintains, has possession of, or causes or permits an animal to be harbored or kept, who has an animal in their care, who shelters or provides food seven consecutive days or longer, or permits an animal to remain on or around their premises. The term "owner" also includes any person hired or acting as custodian of the animal for its owner.
Performing animal exhibition means any spectacle, display, act or event in which performing animals are used, other than circuses.
Pet means any domestic animal legally kept by an owner for the primary purpose of pleasure as opposed to for commercial or agricultural purposes.
Pet dealer means any person/entity who sells, offers to sell, exchanges, or offers for adoption dogs, cats, birds, fish, reptiles, or other customary pets. However, a person who sells only animals that he/she/they has/have produced and raised, not to exceed 30 animals a year, shall not be considered a pet dealer unless such person is licensed for a business by a local government or has a state sales tax number.
Private kennel means entity or person, excluding commercial kennels, pet dealers and vet clinics or hospitals, who keeps, harbors, or knowingly permits to remain on or about their premises, more than six dogs and six cats over four months of age on a property consisting of three acres or less.
Proper enclosure means enclosure for keeping a dangerous or vicious dog on owner's property, securely confined indoors or outdoors in a securely enclosed and locked pen, fence, or structure suitable to prevent entry of young children and designed to prevent the animal from escaping. Any pen or structure shall have secure sides and a secure top, and if the animal is enclosed in a fence, all sides of the fence shall be of sufficient height, and the bottom of the fence shall prevent the animal's escape from either over, under, or through the fence. Any such enclosure shall also provide protection from the elements, fresh food, and water.
Running at-large means on public property and not under the control of a responsible person, or on property other than its owner's without the consent of such other owner.
Sanitary means in clean, healthy condition; hygienic; consistent with normal requirements of the animal's living area, size, species, and breed.
Secure enclosure means locked pen or structure sufficient to prevent an animal from escaping and preventing other animals entering.
Serious injury means any physical injury that creates a substantial risk of death; results in death, broken or dislocated bones, lacerations requiring multiple sutures, or disfiguring avulsions; requires plastic surgery or admission to a hospital; or results in protracted impairment of health, including transmission of an infection or contagious disease, or impairment of function of any bodily organ.
Tethered means attached to a stationary object or pulley system by chain, rope, cable, or similar.
Under control means an animal, secured on the property of the owner or another with consent, which is:
(1) Confined by fence, pen, cage, or secure enclosure to the premises of its owner; or a vehicle.
(2) Secured by leash, chain or lead of sufficient strength to prevent escaping from premises of owner or vehicle.
(3) Under immediate physical control of owner; if a dog immediately heeds owner's verbal commands, it need not be leashed if within sight of owner and responds to verbal commands.
Vaccination means inoculation by authorized person of specified dose of rabies vaccine which has the U.S. government license number approval stamp on the label of the vaccine container.
Veterinarian or vet means any person who holds a license to practice veterinary medicine in the state.
Veterinary clinic or hospital means a clinic or hospital operated by a veterinarian.
Vicious dog means a dog that inflicts serious injury on a person or causes serious injury to a person resulting from reasonable attempts to escape from the dog's attack.
Wild or exotic animals means any wild animal, wildlife, vertebrate or invertebrate recognized by the state as wild animal, wildlife, exotic or hybrid or regulated in O.C.G.A. § 27-5-5 irrespective of actual or asserted state of docility, domesticity, tameness or intended use. Also included in the term "wild or exotic animals" are any animal capable of causing severe injury by means of venoms, poisons, toxins, constriction or bite, and includes, without limitation, any primate, raccoon, skunk, wolf, squirrel, fox, leopard, panther, tiger, lion, lynx, bear, wild rabbit, wild rodent and reptiles, including, but not limited to, crocodiles, alligators, snakes, caiman and gavials, and any other animal so designated by animal control. Specifically excluded from the term "wild or exotic animals" are Psittaciformes, ferrets, miniature pigs, hamsters, guinea pigs, gerbils, chinchilla, dogs, cats, llamas, and non-venomous snakes (boa, python, etc.) less than eight feet.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
415:
This article shall be enforced by county animal control and all duly appointed and qualified law enforcement officers and animal control officers. Animal control is authorized to employ any equipment it deems necessary to enforce this chapter, including, without limit, wire box traps. Animal control may, subject to conditions it may determine, lend such traps or other equipment to private persons for the purpose of preventing nuisances resulting from animals running at-large.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
416:
No person shall interfere with, hinder or prevent an animal control or other law enforcement officer in the performance of duty or seek to release any animal in the custody of animal control or other law enforcement agency. Obstruction of an officer includes, but is not limited to:
(1) Relocating, interfering with, or altering a device, equipment, item, or property used for animal control.
(2) Placing one's animal in or removing any animal confined in a cage used for animal control.
(3) Giving a false name, address, or date of birth to any officer, employee, or agent of the county.
(4) Giving information with intent to mislead an officer, employee, or agent of animal control or the sheriff's department.
(5) Refusing to show proper identification where required by an officer of animal control or the sheriff's department.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
417:
(a) Animal control and law enforcement officers have authority to go on public or private property to investigate and seize and impound animals therein/thereon.
(b) Animal control and law enforcement officers may use force to remove an animal from a closed vehicle for enforcement purposes. The operator of the vehicle may be charged with cruelty. No legal action for property damage or trespass may be had for such use of force.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
418:
Any person in violation of this chapter may be punished by a fine and/or imprisonment, as provided in section 1-7 of this Code. Each day a violation exists shall be a separate offense. Except where inconsistent with mandatory minimum sentences specified in this chapter, the court with jurisdiction over violations of this chapter may suspend the sentence on terms and conditions as it may prescribe for payment of a fine, for community service in lieu of fine or incarceration, for the payment of restitution, or other condition. Where allowed by law, the court may prohibit the offender from owning, possessing, or having on offender's premises, any animal during the term of the sentence, may order the violator to pay boarding fees and restitution for medical treatment and expenses incurred by the county during investigation, and impose other sanctions allowed by law.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
420:
(a) No one may own a wild or exotic animal without a certificate of registration by animal control.
(b) Animal control shall issue a certificate of registration only if the owner presents sufficient evidence of proper licensing by state or federal agencies with an inspection report demonstrating compliance with the housing requirements of O.C.G.A. § 27-5-6.
(c) The owner shall notify animal control if the wild or exotic animal is moving out of the city.
(d) The owner shall register a wild or exotic animal within ten days of moving into the city or the purchase or birth of a new wild or exotic animal.
(e) The owner shall not allow it at-large and must immediately notify animal control of escape.
(f) The owner of a wild or exotic animal that attacks a human must notify animal control immediately.
(g) The owner must notify animal control within 24 hours of transfer of ownership and provide name, address and telephone number of the new owner.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
422:
Domestic animals are allowed only to the extent permitted in this article and applicable city zoning regulations.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
423:
(a) The maximum number of cats and dogs that may be kept shall be as follows: Over three acres: six dogs and six cats. One and one half to three acres: five dogs and five cats. 0.75 to 1.49 acres: four dogs and four cats. Less than 0.75 acres: three dogs and three cats. However, for any dwelling unit in a multi-family development (e.g., apartment, condominium, townhome, mobile home park, duplex, or similar), it shall be unlawful to possess or keep more than two dogs and two cats.
(b) Reserved.
(c) References to dogs and cats only refer to dogs and cats older than 12 weeks. A new litter shall be exempt from the provisions herein for 12 weeks from the date of birth.
(d) If it is determined that a person is in violation of this section, such person shall be allowed 30 days from notice of violation to cure same.
(e) Animal establishments (as defined in this chapter), and licensed veterinarians and veterinary clinics, shall not be subject to this section but shall be subject to zoning requirements applicable to the term "kennels," as defined in the city zoning code.
(Ord. of 2-10-2025(1), § 1(Att. A))
424:
(a) Livestock. The following restrictions are established for keeping livestock such as cattle, horses, and similar animals.
(1) Livestock shall be permitted to be kept in zoning districts AG-G and RR, on properties which are not less than three acres in size.
(2) All buildings used for livestock shall be located at least 200 feet from any property line.
(3) All livestock shall be maintained at least 100 feet from any property line.
(4) There shall be a minimum of 5,000 square feet of fenced lot area not covered by the principal building or structure for each livestock animal.
(5) Live slaughter of livestock shall be prohibited.
(6) It shall be unlawful to keep hogs, swine, or pigs within the city.
(7) All yards or pens wherein livestock are kept shall be regularly covered with lime or other suitable chemical agents, as may be approved by the city code enforcement officer, to prevent bad odors or nuisances to neighbors.
(b) Keeping of fowl and small domestic animals. Small domesticated animals, such as rabbits and guinea pigs, and fowl, such as chickens, ducks and the like, but excluding guineas, geese, and male fowl (such as roosters, toms, drakes, etc.), or other crowing fowl (such as peacocks), may be kept in RR, R1, R2, and R3 zoning districts within the city subject to the following regulations:
(1) No fowl shall be kept on a lot of less than 1,000 square feet.
(2) Except as otherwise provided in section 6-10, the number of small domesticated animals and fowl shall be limited to three such animals per property, which number shall be in addition to the number of animals permitted under section 6-10.
(3) All such animals shall be provided with adequate and sanitary covered housing for roosting and protection. Such houses, hutches, pens, sheds, stalls and enclosures wherein domesticated animals or fowl are kept shall have a solid floor as may be approved by the city code enforcement officer. All such houses, hutches, pens, sheds, stalls and enclosures shall have a minimum floor space of six square feet per animal or bird over one month old.
(4) All houses, hutches, pens, sheds, stalls or enclosures where such small domesticated animals or fowl are kept shall not be nearer to any houses wherein human beings reside, other than the residence of the person who is the owner of such animals, than a distance of 15 feet. All such houses, hutches, pens, sheds, stalls and enclosures shall be located in the rear of the yard.
(5) Small domesticated animals or fowl in the city must at all times be kept within a fenced or enclosed area and no person shall fail to prevent his or her animals or fowl from straying from the property of the owner or keeper, or going upon the property of any other person, or upon any public rights-of-way.
(6) Sanitary requirements.
a. It shall be unlawful for any person owning or having control of the use of any house, hutch, pen, stall or enclosure or other place where domesticated animals or fowl are kept, to allow the same to become filthy or unsanitary. Every person who owns or keeps such domesticated animals or fowl shall maintain in connection therewith a bin, pit or container in which the manure from such animals or fowl shall be placed pending removal. Such bin, pit or container shall be provided with covers or other devices, sufficient to prevent the ingress and egress of flies and other insect pests. All persons controlling such places where domesticated animals or fowl are kept shall remove all manure from such bins, pits or containers before the same shall become malodorous or unsanitary. However, any such person may use decomposed manure upon his or her premises for the purpose of enriching his own ground.
b. Houses, hutches, pens, stalls and enclosures where domesticated animals or fowl are kept shall be kept free from vermin.
